title: Ordinary henselization as a limit of residue-preserving affine etale neighbourhoods
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $x\in X$ correspond to a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, with residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. There exist a henselian local $A$-algebra $H$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], a nonempty directed set $I$, and a directed system of $A$-algebras $A_a$ with colimit $H$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], such that each $u_a:\operatorname{Spec}A_a\to X$ is separated etale of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and has a chosen point $x_a$ over $x$ inducing an isomorphism $\kappa(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(x_a)$. The transition maps preserve these points and their residue-field identifications. The induced map $\operatorname{Spec}H\to\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ takes the closed point to $x_a$; the map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to H$ is local, $\mathfrak pH$ is the maximal ideal, and $\kappa(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}H/\mathfrak pH$. Moreover $\operatorname{Spec}H\cong\varprojlim_a\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ over $X$.

source.place: Tag 04GN (lemma-henselization), statement (1)--(4) and proof: colimit of etale algebras pointed with unchanged residue field; apply to A_p and descend finite etale presentations to principal neighbourhoods in Spec A. Directed reindexing of the small filtered diagram, and affine spectrum of its colimit.

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(x)$. Consider the etale residue triples over $(A,\mathfrak p,k,\mathrm{id}_k)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-residue-triples]. For $t=(B_t,\alpha_t,q_t,\phi_t)$ the composite $k\to\kappa(q_t)\xrightarrow{\phi_t}k$ is the identity. Since both maps are field embeddings, they are inverse isomorphisms: for $z\in\kappa(q_t)$, injectivity of $\phi_t$ gives $z=i(\phi_t(z))$. Thus every object already has the required unchanged residue field, with no separable-closure hypothesis. Choose a small full representative category $\mathcal T$: [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover] gives a set of underlying affine etale schemes and, for each, the triples of primes and field maps form a set. Transport of objects and arrows along representative isomorphisms preserves filteredness and all pointings.

source.place: Tag 04GN (lemma-henselization), category of residue-preserving pairs; Tag 04GW, pointed-triple description; size bound from topologies.tex Tag 04HR.

proof.text: The category $\mathcal T$ is filtered by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-triples-filtered-colimit-filtered], applied with the arbitrary field $K=k$ and $\chi=\mathrm{id}$. Take the colimit $H$ of its diagram of commutative $A$-algebras using [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist]. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise], it is also the colimit in commutative rings and every element comes from a stage. The compatible pointings $\psi_t:B_t\to k$ induce $\psi:H\to k$ by the colimit universal property; write $\iota_t:B_t\to H$ for the legs and $\rho:A\to H$ for the structural map. Thus $\psi\iota_t=\psi_t$ and $\iota_t\alpha_t=\rho$. Reindex by [lem-coef-cardinal-filtered-poset-reindex] with $\eta=\aleph_0$, obtaining a nonempty directed poset $I$ and a diagram $A_a=B_{u(a)}$ with the same colimit $H$. Retain the original legs $\iota_t$ for all $t$, as well as the restricted legs.

source.place: Tag 04GN (lemma-henselization), filtered colimit construction; categories.tex Tag 0032 (lemma-directed-category-system) for directed reindexing.

proof.text: For $h\in H$, choose $h=\iota_t(b)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]. If $\psi(h)\ne0$, then $b\notin q_t$, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-triple-unit-refinement] gives a pointed successor where $b$ is a unit; its image in $H$ is $h$ by cocone naturality, hence $h$ is a unit. If $\psi(h)=0$, then $b\in q_t$, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-triple-ideal-refinement] gives a successor where $b$ belongs to $\mathfrak pB_s$; mapping its finite ideal expression to $H$ gives $h\in\mathfrak pH$. Conversely $\psi\rho$ kills $\mathfrak p$, hence $\mathfrak pH\subseteq\ker\psi$. Therefore $\ker\psi=\mathfrak pH$ and every element outside this proper ideal is a unit.

source.place: Tag 04GN (lemma-henselization), paragraphs proving locality, ideal equality and residue field; ideal refinement uses Tag 00U4 (lemma-etale-at-prime).

proof.text: Set $\mathfrak m=\ker\psi=\mathfrak pH$. Every proper ideal of $H$ lies in $\mathfrak m$, since elements outside it are units, so $H$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. For $s\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$, $\psi\rho(s)\ne0$, hence $\rho(s)$ is invertible. The fraction formula $a/s\mapsto\rho(a)\rho(s)^{-1}$ defines $A_{\mathfrak p}\to H$: the fraction relation is preserved after multiplying by the images of its denominators. Its inverse image of $\mathfrak m$ is $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$, because its composite with $\psi$ is the usual map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to k$. It is therefore local. Every $z\in k=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$ has the form $\bar a/\bar s$, $s\notin\mathfrak p$, so $z=\psi(\rho(a)\rho(s)^{-1})$. Thus $\psi$ is surjective and induces $H/\mathfrak m\cong k$, inverse to the map from $A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}=k$.

source.place: Tag 04GN (lemma-henselization), locality and residue-field paragraphs, applied directly to the system over A; localization is Definition Tag 00CO.

proof.text: Let $P\in H[T]$ be monic and let $a_0\in k$ satisfy $\overline P(a_0)=0$ and $\overline{P'}(a_0)\ne0$. Use [lemma-nagata-filtered-colimit-finite-data] on its finitely many coefficients to obtain a monic $Q\in A_a[T]$ mapping to $P$ (lift the coefficients below the leading term and set that term equal to $1$). Put $B=A_a$ and use its pointing $B\to k$. Then $Q(a_0)=0$ and $Q'(a_0)\ne0$ in $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative], $E=B[T,Y]/(Q,YQ'-1)$ is etale over $B$ and has a $B$-algebra map $E\to k$ with $T\mapsto a_0$. Composition makes $E$ etale over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The kernel $q_E$ of $E\to k$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$; the map extends to a field embedding $\kappa(q_E)\to k$ since every denominator outside $q_E$ maps to a nonzero element. Hence $E$ defines a triple $s$ and $B\to E$ a pointed arrow from $u(a)$ to $s$, after transport to representatives. The cocone equation $\iota_s\circ(B\to E)=\iota_{u(a)}$ gives $P(\iota_s(T))=0$ and $\psi(\iota_s(T))=a_0$.

source.place: Tag 04GN (lemma-henselization), final paragraph adjoining a simple root; standard etale algebra: Definition Tag 00UB and Lemma Tag 00UC.

proof.text: The simple-root lifting condition proved in Step 5 and the local-ring structure of Step 4 satisfy condition (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting]. Its implication (ii) to (i) proves that $H$ is henselian in exactly the idempotent-lifting sense of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. This supplies the requested henselian local $A$-algebra.

source.place: Definition Tag 04GF (definition-henselian), Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian); more-algebra.tex Tag 09XI identifies the idempotent convention.

proof.text: For every $a$, let $x_a=q_{u(a)}$. Step 1 gives $\kappa(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(x_a)$. The triple morphisms preserve their pointings, so their inverse-image prime ideals and residue identifications are preserved. The map $\psi\iota_{u(a)}$ has kernel $q_{u(a)}$, while $\ker\psi=\mathfrak m$; consequently $\iota_{u(a)}^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=q_{u(a)}$, so the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}H$ maps to $x_a$. Each $u_a:\operatorname{Spec}A_a\to X$ is etale by the definition of a triple. It is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated] and of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1): its source is affine, its target $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and etaleness includes local finite presentation. These hypotheses do not require $A$ to be Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 04GN (lemma-henselization), pointed etale system; schemes.tex Tags 01KN and 01KV for separatedness, Tag 03GI for quasi-compactness; morphisms.tex Definition 01TP for finite presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit] to the small ring diagram $a\mapsto A_a$ and its colimit cocone with vertex $H$. It identifies $\operatorname{Spec}H$ with $\varprojlim_a\operatorname{Spec}A_a$, with precisely the spectrum maps of the coprojections as projections. All maps commute with the maps to $X$ because every transition and every coprojection is an $A$-algebra map. The same cone is therefore limiting over $X$: a cone over $X$ has its unique factorization in schemes, and composing that factorization with any projection shows it is over $X$ (the index set is nonempty). Together with $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pH$ and the residue identification of Step 4, this proves every clause.

source.place: Tag 01YW (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit), affine spectrum of the colimit and its projections.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q36-7f8bfbfb4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 26 stmt_dep/proof_dep statements and Stacks algebra.tex 04GN (lemma-henselization) statement and proof in full. Statement unchanged; the one addition is the stmt_dep def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, which A_p needs. There are no new nodes. The route matches 04GN, carried out over A with triples pointed into k=kappa(p), which avoids the false claim that A->A_p is etale. Step 1: phi∘i=id plus injectivity makes the residue maps isomorphisms; the essentially-small cover gives the small model. Step 2: filteredness for arbitrary K, colimit plus elementwise, psi from the cocone, reindexing at aleph_0 to a nonempty directed poset. The reindex lemma holds for every category C, so it gives the ring colimit that Steps 5 and 8 need. Step 3: unit and ideal refinements give ker psi = pH (elementary). Step 4: locality, A_p->H is local, and psi is surjective via fractions (needed for nonmaximal p). Step 5: monic Q lifted by finite data; standard-etale (2) with L=k gives E->k, T->a_0, with no lift needed; q_E and the compatible residue map make E a triple. Step 6: root lifting (ii)=>(i) gives idempotent henselian. Step 7: iota^{-1}(m)=q_{u(a)}; transition maps preserve points and identifications; separated because the source is affine; finite presentation from qcqs-permanence (1). Step 8: the Spec-colimit limit, over X. Edge cases checked: a field A, (0) in Z, k[eps]/eps^2, non-Noetherian A. Duplicate search over henselization, 04GN and pair/strict-henselization nodes found none that states pointed residue-preserving A-neighbourhoods. tool_uses accepted (generic algebra tools); the 'Fourier unit' wording in them is cosmetic.
